text:
Bobby Brink is the hometown kid from Minnetonka now playing for the Wild, and his November has had an edge to it. Markerzone.com reported Charlie McAvoy faced a possible suspension after a fight with Brink in Minnesota's rout of Boston, and the Pioneer Press ran "For Wild's Bobby Brink, the fire is rising." The Duluth News Tribune wrote he found "another level" on the recent road trip.

The production is modest so far, 11 points (2 goals) in 24 games at 13.6 minutes a night, and the goals are the part that's lagging. He has just two on 5.01 expected goals (the quality of chances), shooting 5.3%, far below his usual range. He keeps getting the looks, and goals tend to follow chances. Markerzone even caught him taking it out on his stick after a missed 3-on-1 against Toronto.

The rest of the picture is solid. Minnesota takes 56% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on, and his ice time is up over his last ten games. Evolving-Hockey had him slightly above replacement level last season in Philadelphia, mostly for his defensive work. We'd watch whether the shooting percentage drifts back toward normal.
